resolutions.keyAt: The box of apples is heavy.
resolutions.note: The reviewer is describing the language honestly: over an intervening prepositional phrase, the plural verb is what most children hear at home, and a descriptive linguist would not call it an error. But that is precisely what CCSS L.3.1f asks a grade-3 child to learn — subject-verb agreement when a phrase stands between the subject and its verb — so the common spoken form is the RIGHT distractor here, not a second answer. A question whose wrong option is the mistake it exists to catch is the question working. Distinct from the calendar/heighth cases, where a dictionary recorded the rejected option as correct for the very thing the stem asked; no reference work calls 'Each of the girls have' the standard written form. All three sit at level 4, the stretch rung, which is where this belongs.
